## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rāja Sutta* (*Rājasutta*, Ud 2.2) is the second discourse of the *Mucalindavagga* in the *Udāna* [Ud 2.2]. In the post-enlightenment narrative chronology, it immediately succeeds the *Mucalinda Sutta* at a point where the textual progression of the *Udāna* diverges from that of the *Vinaya Mahākhandhaka* [Anandajoti 2010]. In this discourse, the Buddha encounters a group of monks gossiping about kings and worldly affairs, admonishing them that engaging in political conversation is inappropriate for renunciants; when monks gather, their only proper pursuits are righteous conversation (*dhammakathā*) or noble silence (*ariyam tuṇhībhāva*) [eJournal of Buddhist Research Studies 2015].

 The text is also cited in early paracanonical exegesis, including the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2) and the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37). Computational analysis via DharmaNexus reveals high internal text reuse with other *Udāna* suttas framing inappropriate monastic chatter, notably the *Piṇḍapātika Sutta* (Ud 3.8) and *Sippa Sutta* (Ud 3.9), as well as formulaic stock passages shared across the *Nikāyas* (such as AN 4, AN 10, DN 14, and MN 119) and aligned with Chinese Āgama texts and the Sanskrit *Mahāvadānasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
